findings.title: Plain `nio check tasks` now accepts unrated tasks, so only the optional flag stops them
quotes: if "Tier" in f and f["Tier"] != "to be rated":
findings.fix: make `tasks.check` itself report any Tier or Mode containing `to be rated`, behind the existing gate or approval path. Keep `--rated-from` only for the diff check.

sources.situation: the diff exempts a Tier value of `to be rated` from validation in `tasks.check`. The drafter card writes `strong: to be rated`, and the `TIER` regex already accepts that as tier `strong` with reason "to be rated". So `nio check tasks <slug>` and `--approved` (which gates the implement stage) pass a `tasks.md` the evaluator never touched. The only detector is the substring test in `rated_from`, and it runs only when the skill's step 3 passes `--rated-from`. If the evaluator step is skipped or fails, or a human runs `nio check tasks --approved`, unrated tasks reach implement with no error and no warning.

findings.reason: FR-9, AC-26/27 and CT-7 define the rejection of unrated tasks only for `nio check tasks --rated-from`; CT-11 and AC-28 make the tasks skill pass that flag after the evaluator. No requirement says plain `nio check tasks` or `--approved` must reject `to be rated`, so asking for that goes beyond this spec.

findings.title: Evaluator-left default `Effort: med` is undetectable, and the dead exact-match exemption is a silent-pass path
quotes: elif rating(b) and "to be rated" in b:
findings.fix: require that each task's Tier and Mode line differ from the copy, or that no placeholder text remains. Say plainly that Effort can't be proven rated.

sources.situation: the drafter card leaves `Effort:` as `med`, a valid value. If the evaluator skips a task's Effort, the old and new lines are equal, the line contains no `to be rated`, and AC-27 passes with that task silently unrated. The same applies if the evaluator rewrites only some tasks' Tier lines: a task whose line is unchanged but still `strong: to be rated` is caught only by the substring match, not by "was rated".

A task is left unrated and the skill's step 4 `nio check tasks <slug>` runs without `--rated-from`. It now accepts `to be rated` for both Tier and Mode, so only the `--rated-from` run catches an unrated task. No AC or test covers this relaxation of the plain check.

findings.title: A stale or missing copy is accepted or crashes
findings.fix: turn the open failure into a `ValueError` or an `ERROR` line. State that the copy must sit under `.nio/runs/<run>/`.

sources.situation: `rated_from` trusts the path it is given. If the agent copies `tasks.md` after the evaluator ran, or copies it twice, the diff is empty and the check passes whatever the evaluator changed. A nonexistent copy raises `FileNotFoundError`, which `cli.py` doesn't catch (it catches only `ValueError`), so the output is a traceback instead of an `ERROR` line. AC-28's test only checks the word order in the skill text.

findings.title: The tasks skill starts its run with a form the CLI refuses
quotes: give the stage or task too: nio run <slug> <stage|T-n>
findings.fix: change the step to "Start a run with `nio run`" (bare, as CT-11 and the other skills say), or, if the slug is wanted, `nio run <slug> tasking`.

sources.situation: the tasks agent follows step 3 as written and runs `nio run <slug>`. `cli.py` exits with "error: give the stage or task too", so no `.nio/runs/<run>/` exists and the `tasks.before.md` copy has nowhere to go. Even with a second argument, `tasks` is not a stage (`flow.py` STAGES names `tasking`). CT-11 says the step "starts a run with `nio run`", with no slug, and plan, spec and jury all use bare `nio run`.

findings.reason: skills/tasks/SKILL.md step 3 says "Start a run with `nio run <slug>`", but cli.py lines 186-188 exit with "give the stage or task too" when a slug has no target. CT-11 says step 3 "starts a run with `nio run`" (bare), so the skill text contradicts the CLI and the contract.

findings.title: Nothing forces the evaluator to rate Mode, so a skipped Mode passes both checks
quotes: Leave `Tier:` and `Effort:` as `strong: to be rated` and `med`
`if "Mode" in f and f["Mode"] != "to be rated":`
findings.fix: have the drafter write `- Mode: to be rated` (and the template to match), and have `rated_from` (or `check`) fail a Mode line still equal to the drafter's copy. A test should cover a Mode left unrated.

sources.situation: the drafter card names only Tier and Effort for the sentinel, so the drafter leaves `- Mode: split: <why>` from the template. If the evaluator skips that line, `nio check tasks` passes it (`split` is a valid mode and `<why>` is a non-empty reason), and `rated_from` passes it too, because it looks only for the text "to be rated". The run then ends with a task whose Mode was never rated, though the skill says the evaluator sets it and D-261029-rkpb says the task is worked in the rated mode.

findings.reason: FR-9 and AC-27 require only that non-rating lines stay unchanged and that no line still reads `to be rated`. Nothing requires the evaluator's Mode edit to be detectable, and CT-7 says nothing about a drafter `Mode: to be rated` sentinel. The finding asks for a requirement the spec doesn't have.
findings.where: src/nio/agents/tasks-drafter.md line 35; src/nio/templates/tasks.md line 34; src/nio/tasks.py:223-228 and 302-313

findings.title: The rating guard compares a sentinel the drafter never writes, and the tests use that form
quotes: `if "Tier" in f and f["Tier"] != "to be rated":`
findings.fix: compare the reason part, for example `TIER.match(f["Tier"])[2] != "to be rated"`, and use `strong: to be rated` in the `rated_run` fixture.

sources.situation: the drafter writes `- Tier: strong: to be rated`. The guard compares the whole value to the bare text "to be rated", so it never skips the line. `check` then reads `strong` with reason `to be rated` as a finished rating. Only `rated_from`'s substring test catches it. The `rated_run` fixture in `test_tasks.py` uses the bare form, which the drafter never writes, so no test covers the real placeholder.

findings.title: A missing or unreadable copy crashes the check with a traceback
quotes: rel, new, old = p.relative_to(root), p.read_text().splitlines(), open(copy).read().splitlines()
findings.fix: raise ValueError for a missing copy, or return an error line, so the existing `error:` path or the `ERROR` output handles it.

sources.situation: `nio check tasks <slug> --rated-from <path>` is run with a path that does not exist, for example when the skill failed to make the copy. `open(copy)` raises FileNotFoundError. The CLI only catches ValueError, so the human sees a traceback and not an `ERROR` line with `N errors`.
